name: Centro de Datos Alcalá (Alcalá Data Center)

profile.reading: This is Telefonicas Centro de Datos Alcala, in Alcala de Henares in the Madrid metropolitan area, one of the companys flagship large scale Spanish data centers per Telefonicas own published fact sheet for the site. The building totals about 75,000 square meters, or roughly 807,000 square feet, of which about 15,000 square meters, or roughly 161,000 square feet, is usable technical space, organized into independent modular rooms of about 681 square meters each. The facility is fed by a dedicated electrical substation delivering up to 100 megawatts of capacity, uses free cooling with isothermal cisterns, and is backed by diesel generators, holding Uptime Institute Tier IV Gold certification for 99.995 percent uptime alongside PCI DSS, ISO 20000, ISO 27001, ISO 14001, LEED, and Spanish LOPD and Esquema Nacional de Seguridad compliance. Telefonica markets the site for managed and outsourced cloud infrastructure, hosting, and disaster recovery services across Spain and Europe, with synchronous replication to two of the companys other data centers and connectivity to about 100 points of presence in more than 40 countries over roughly 45,000 kilometers of fiber. Telefonica itself was founded April 19, 1924 in Madrid as Compania Telefonica Nacional de Espana, with ITT among its founding shareholders, and operated as Spains sole telephone operator under majority Spanish state ownership, roughly 79.6 percent from 1945, until the market liberalized in 1997. Today the company operates globally under the Movistar, O2, and Vivo brands, reporting roughly 100,870 employees and more than 44.7 billion dollars in revenue in 2024. Telefonica lists Alcala de Henares among its handful of largest strategic Spanish data center sites, historically distinguishing it from the companys smaller regional network facilities, and the citys own long history as a university and administrative center in the Madrid region made it an established location for large scale institutional and telecommunications infrastructure well before this specific data center was built.
